episode.episode: Philips Hue: The smart home’s light bulb moment
episode.showDescription: Version History is a show about the best gadgets ever. And the worst ones. And the ones that might have changed the world, if they ever actually shipped. Every week, your favorite people from The Verge and beyond hang out to tell and debate the story of a gadget, app, website, or any other tech product, and try to determine the item’s true legacy. Because not every product is a hit, but every product has a story. And the ones that really matter aren’t always the ones you think. From the Verge and the Vox Media Podcast Network.
episode.episodeDescription: The humble light bulb might be the ultimate success story in the smart home. Our connected, adaptable homes are supposed to be customizable, connected to everything, and incredibly easy to use, and nothing has made that work quite like Philips Hue lights. In this episode, The Verge's David Pierce and Jennifer Pattison Tuohy are joined by smart home journalist and expert Richard Gunther to tell the Hue's story. We trace the product's history from its origins in the smartphone revolution, try to figure out how Philips managed to turn a staggeringly expensive lightbulb into a must-have gadget, and look at whether there's even more invention left in the future of lighting. We’re also on video! Check us out on YouTube. Subscribe to The Verge for unlimited access to theverge.com, subscriber-exclusive newsletters, and our ad-free podcast feed. We love hearing from you! transcript_window.text: And as they were trying to develop this, they spun out this team to be just focused on this, what was essentially a software project.
And then as they started to develop it, they realized this was a really core idea.
And if you kept it just in a lamp, you were really limiting its use case because you'd have to buy lots of lamps.
Whereas Whereas if they could put it into a form factor where you could have it throughout your home, it would have so much more potential.
And so then they went back into Philips, into another team and got this team.
It's like, OK, can we build this?
Can we build this light?
Can we build a light bulb that can be controlled?
And I will pop quiz for you, Richard.
What was the protocol that the living color lamps used?
Do you know?
How far back does your protocol knowledge go?
I know.
Okay.
I have no idea.
I'll be honest.
I would have found it incredibly alarming if you had known the answer to that question off the top of your head.
I think it's for the best.
Jen, what was it?
So it was the early Zigbee Lightlink.
They call it SmartLink.
And it actually, they ended up, so Philips ended up developing and donating to Zigbee what is today Lightlink.
And that is a huge part.
I mean, you're familiar with Zigbee LightLink, right, Richard?
I am, actually.
Yeah, it's funny.
